The Weekly Cybers #136

OpenAI’s Medicare hack highlights dodgy government cybersecurity, Anthropic’s US$2 trillion IPO prospectus leaked, and Australian researchers get AI models “drunk” so they spill the tea.

Actual Article Body:
2 October 2026

Or so says Donald Trump, and he’d know.

It’s yet another week when AI safety dominates the cyber news. There’s the fallout from OpenAI’s hack of Medicare and many others. And there’s Anthropic’s US$2 trillion IPO prospectus, which was leaked to Reuters, and which of course warns of existential risks.

A story that particularly amused me was Transport for London spending £320,000 on live facial recognitions camera which led to just one ID — and even that was a false positive. Such a glorious waste!

In two decades of writing about cybersecurity there’s been a constant theme: everyone has outdated legacy systems with vulnerabilities that have long since been forgotten.

So in the wake of OpenAI’s hack of Medicare that we spoke about last week, it came as no surprise to hear that, yes, Australia is run on legacy systems that AI agents can easily exploit.

“They aren’t updated and maintained because either people have forgotten about them or it’s too costly, or there aren’t updates for systems anymore. That creates an enormous vulnerability, and that is what these agents are going to be exploiting,” said Johanna Weaver, head of the Tech Policy Design Institute.

It also came as no surprise that the Department of Home Affairs has ordered a government-wide stocktake of legacy systems, to be completed in six months.

“Entities must develop a legacy technology risk management plan, set targets for reducing legacy systems, and apply security patches more rapidly,” reports iTnews.

This should be easy, of course. Each organisation can simply refer to the up-to-date list of their computing assets, along with their replacement timeline and budget — lol no of course they won’t be able to do that.

We’ll find out more about this stocktake later this month.

Oh, and it isn’t surprising that government ministers were warned months ago about this sort of vulnerability. No one ever listens.

Meanwhile we’ve learned that the data accessed by OpenAI’s AI cyber robot swarm included internal files and credentials, so that’s definitely a worry.

OpenAI has apologised, and scrapped the release of their next model, GPT-6.1 Astra, over safety concerns. Nevertheless they did release Dots, their new series of autonomous AI agents.

Everything is fine.

Anthropic’s confidential IPO filing was leaked to Reuters. It values the company at more than US$2 trillion, even though the company lost US$42 billion in 2025.

The company, which makes the Claude series of large language models, plans to spend $518 billion on cloud, computing, and infrastructure in the coming years, Reuters reports.

Anthropic currently relies on a small number of clients, including key big-tech partners. Amazon and Google’s parent Alphabet together accounted for 47% of 2025 sales, for example.

And of course the prospectus warns that AI may pose “existential risks to humanity”.

Finance professor Patrick Boyle has posted one of his highly entertaining videos looking at whether the AI boom is a bubble, and what you would have to believe to pay AU$2 trillion for an AI lab.

YOU CAN HAVE ME FOR LESS THAN $2 TRILLION: Yes, I too am seeking your investment. This newsletter is free to read, but it’s unfunded. Crowdfunding also fuels my podcasts The 9pm Edict and Another Untitled Music Podcast. It’d be lovely if you threw a few dollars into the tip jar at stilgherrian.com/tip, or supported this season’s podcast crowdfunder. If you’ve already done so, thank you very much.

LATEST PODCAST: In The 9pm Space Dust of Disappointment with Dr Alice Gorman and Rami Mandow, space archaeologist and astrophysicist respectively, we discuss the US admission that it has weapons in space, how planets and asteroids and their features get their names, Millisecond Pulsar PSR J0437-4715, whether alien civilisations are hiding in Moon dust, the Bepicolombo mission to Mercury, and much more. Look for The 9pm Edict in your podcast app.
